A second investigator, starting fresh with the same tools, tested the kind of each fault in your draft answer. Their findings:

### `ts-travel2-service`: you said `database_call_failed`. They conclude `network_partition` (confidence: medium).
Scope: Affected: every travel2 operation that needs its MySQL connection (Hikari pool acquisition, TripRepository.findAll, Travel2Controller.queryInfo, POST trips/left and trips/routes), which in the incident all hang about 30 s and fail, and the calls from route-plan and travel-plan that depend on them. Not affected by the fault: the ts-travel2-service pod itself, which keeps emitting spans and logs at a reduced rate, and its non-DB traffic, which is absent in the incident rather than observed failing. The MySQL side has no spans, so I cannot tell from this data which end of the link is cut.
Ruled out:
- `database_call_failed`: The claimed kind is rejected. Its errors are connection-level (Communications link failure, no packets received, SQLState 08S01 and 08003, No operations allowed after connection closed, Hikari connection not available after 30000ms), not SQL-layer throws on particular statements; every DB-touching span fails together with none succeeding, so there is no contrast between failing and working statements.
- `database_call_slow`: The about 30 s on the DB-named spans is a wait for a pooled connection and a hang to timeout, not steady extra self-reported execution time on particular statements; the connection-level errors and the total failure of the connection do not fit a steady slowdown.
- `application_exception`: The errors are driver and pool errors (Hikari, MySQL communications), not application-code exceptions escaping the handler; the SEVERE lines are Spring wrappers around CannotCreateTransactionException and DataAccessResourceFailureException caused by the connection failure.
- `pod_unavailable`: ts-travel2-service keeps emitting spans (about 10.7 per minute) and logs (about 24.7 per minute) in the incident, and its Server spans still return errors rather than vanishing, so the instance is not gone.
- `dns_lookup_failed`: No name-resolution text (UnknownHost, no such host, name resolution) appears in the travel2 logs; the failures are link-level, after connections were made.
- `network_delay`: Calls do not succeed slowly; the DB calls fail at the 30 s timeout and nothing succeeds at a higher latency, so this is a cut rather than added latency on a live link.
Evidence:
- In the incident, TripRepository.findAll (12 spans), Travel2Controller.queryInfo (12), SELECT travel2.entity.Trip (1), POST trips/left Server (12) and POST trips/routes Server (1) all take about 30,000 ms and every one is an error, against about 1.9 ms with zero errors for findAll in the normal period; the SELECT ts.trip2 client statement (660 calls, 0.24 ms normal) has no abnormal row at all, so the whole DB path went quiet or failed together rather than particular statements failing.

- Incident errors are connection-level: 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms' (22 ERROR), 'Communications link failure ... The driver has not received any packets from the server' (20 ERROR), 'SQL Error: 0, SQLState: 08S01' (20 WARN), 'SQL Error: 0, SQLState: 08003' and 'No operations allowed after connection closed' from 23:07:05 on, and repeated 'Failed to validate connection' warnings from 23:06:45. The normal period has only ERROR lines about route-not-found, none about the DB link.

**Verdict: `database_call_failed` is not supported. The evidence points to a network fault on the travel2→MySQL link, most likely the `network_partition` / `network_loss` class (scored as one answer). Confidence: moderate.**

**Why the claim fails**

- **The errors are connection-level, not SQL-layer.** The travel2 logs in the incident are `Communications link failure … The driver has not received any packets from the server`, `SQLState 08S01`, `SQL Error: 0, SQLState: 08003`, `No operations allowed after connection closed`, and `HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms`. The boundary rules say connection-level errors (link failure, connect or read timeout, no connection available) point to the network. `database_call_failed` is reserved for an exception thrown by the SQL layer on particular statements.
- **Every DB-touching path fails the same way, and none succeeds.** In the incident, all 12 `TripRepository.findAll` spans, 12 `Travel2Controller.queryInfo` spans and 12 `POST …/trips/left` Server spans take about 30 s and error. The `SELECT travel2.entity.Trip` span also takes about 30 s, and the `SELECT ts.trip2` client statement (660 calls in the normal period at 0.24 ms) is absent in the incident. Nothing shows a steady extra cost on one statement with the rest of the connection normal. That is the shape of the whole connection failing, not a single statement failing.
- **The time is spent waiting, not executing.** The DB-named spans take about 30 s, matching the Hikari timeout. The lead's "about 30 s" is therefore a wait for a pooled connection and a hang until timeout, not self-reported execution time. That is the signature the boundary rules list for a network fault on the link.
- **The travel2 service is alive.** It still emits about 10.7 spans/min and 24.7 logs/min in the incident, and no restart or uptime break is in the survey. So this is not a pod fault, and the connection is cut rather than the pod gone.
- **The callers see the same 30 s.** The route-plan and travel-plan callers see about 30 s on their Client spans, and travel2's Server spans are also about 30 s with its own time about 30 s. The time is lost inside travel2 at the DB wait, not on the caller-to-travel2 wire.

**What the evidence does not establish**

- Telemetry cannot separate `network_partition` from `network_loss` here, and the evaluator scores them the same. Partition fits better because the calls hang until timeout and the logs show "no packets received", not a probabilistic drop.
- The MySQL side has no spans, and the survey's mysql metrics show a node-utilisation shift I did not chase. I cannot tell from this data whether the link failure is on the travel2 side or on mysql's side.
- The DB-connection and restart metric queries returned no rows (the metric-name filter matched nothing), so pool metrics (`db.client.connections.*`) could not be checked. I did not check `ts-travel-service`, which also shows a drop in spans.
